q: Does the mean-field ODE core reproduce single-cell p53 pulse heterogeneity (Geva-Zatorsky-style bimodal / asynchronous pulsing) once the Haseltine-Rawlings stochastic layer is added, or does the model, even in its full hybrid form, still produce over-synchronized population traces relative to real MCF-7/U-2 OS live-cell imaging?
basis: The paper's Figs. 2 and 3 report mean+/-IQR over 1000 cells but do not compare pulse-timing variance or asynchrony coefficient against Geva-Zatorsky (2010, Mol Syst Biol 2006/2010) single-cell data. Our replication is mean-field-only and therefore cannot answer this. The over-parameterized shared-parameter architecture (all 1000 cells drawn from identical rate constants) is a known source of artificial synchrony.
next_steps: Implement the MOESM2 Haseltine-Rawlings scheme, run 1000-cell simulations, compute (a) coefficient of variation of first-pulse peak time, (b) auto-correlation decay of p53n(t), (c) fraction of cells showing >=2 vs 1 vs 0 pulses in 24 h. Compare against Geva-Zatorsky et al. and Purvis et al. (2012) 4-Gy MCF-7 imaging data. If synchrony is too high, add per-cell log-normal parameter jitter (sigma ~ 0.2 on Wip1 and Mdm2 production rates) and re-test.

q: How does the model behave under S-phase-specific stress where ATR/CHK1 (not ATM/CHK2) is the dominant DDR kinase --- and is the current ATM-only architecture even applicable to replication-stress agents (hydroxyurea, aphidicolin, low-dose gemcitabine) that clinicians actually combine with radiotherapy?
basis: The paper models only the ATM->CHK2->p53 axis. ATR/CHK1 is not in the network at all (MOESM1 Table 1 lists no ATR/CHK1 species). Real DDR involves ATM-ATR crosstalk (Cimprich & Cortez 2008; Blackford & Jackson 2017) that strongly modulates p53 in S phase. This limits the model to G1/G0 DSB-only scenarios --- a substantial scope restriction the paper does not flag.
next_steps: Extend the ODE system with a minimal ATR/CHK1 module (5-6 additional states: ATR, ATRp, CHK1, CHK1p, CDC25A, plus a replication-fork stress input R_s analogous to R_a). Parameterize from Lyu et al. (2019 iScience) or Wortel et al. (2017 Trends Cell Biol). Test whether the extended model reproduces (i) p53 stabilization under HU alone, (ii) synergy vs antagonism with IR when cells are S-phase-synchronized. Compare against published HU+IR clonogenic data (Powell et al., Iliakis lab).

q: Are the fitted parameter values quantitatively identifiable, or are they in fact one point of a large equivalence class producing indistinguishable p53 and NF-kB trajectories --- and if the latter, which of the paper's mechanistic conclusions (Wip1 as the dominant DDR switch-off, TNF-alpha radio-protection via NF-kB) actually survive an identifiability analysis?
basis: The model has ~110 rate constants against a handful of Western-blot time-course readouts plus one clonogenic curve. This is textbook non-identifiability territory (Raue et al. 2009 Bioinformatics profile-likelihood methodology; Villaverde 2019 review). MOESM8 reports local sensitivity plots but not profile likelihoods or Fisher information. Our replication inherits this weakness --- we hit the same trajectories but cannot claim the same mechanism.
next_steps: Run profile-likelihood analysis on the deterministic core (dMod or PEtab-style pipeline in Python) fitting only the western-blot time-course data (Fig. 2, Fig. 3 top rows). Compute confidence intervals for the four 'signature' parameters: k_wip1 (Wip1 production), k_mdm2 (Mdm2 production), k_deg_p53 (Mdm2-dependent p53 degradation), k_ikk (IKK activation). Perform a mechanism-preserving reparameterization test: does raising k_mdm2 while lowering k_wip1 (compensating knob) reproduce the Wip1-RNAi phenotype? If yes, the 'Wip1 is dominant switch-off' claim is not identifiable from these data.

q: How does the model behave at low, physiologically-relevant IR doses (0.05-0.5 Gy, single-DSB regime) where DSB formation is stochastic Poisson and cell-fate is dominated by rare-event dynamics rather than smooth mean-field averaging --- and does the mean-field core meaningfully underestimate low-dose hypersensitivity (LDHS, 'HRS')?
basis: The paper's dose sweep starts at 2 Gy and treats DSB count as a continuous quantity (ma1 * dose / repair_rate ~ 2.3 mean-field DSBs at 4 Gy vs 24 stochastic). At <= 0.5 Gy the discrete-vs-continuous gap is qualitative --- cells either see 0 DSBs or 1-2 DSBs, with no smooth intermediate. Published low-dose hyper-radiosensitivity (Joiner, Marples, Lambin 2001; Prise & O'Sullivan review) is not addressed. Our claim #13 gap is a warning sign here.
next_steps: Extend the Haseltine-Rawlings hybrid to explicitly Poisson-sample DSB creation events at doses 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0 Gy. Compute per-cell apoptotic decision under Kracikova thresholds and plot survival curve. Compare (a) shape (LQ vs induced-repair) against Marples & Joiner 1993 V79 data, (b) whether the p53-pulse count distribution shows the bimodality Bakkenist & Kastan (2003) predicted for single-DSB signalling. If mean-field misses LDHS, argue for stochastic-first analysis at low dose.

q: How does the model's cell-fate landscape shift when key p53-pathway genes are mutated in a tumor-cell-line-specific way (TP53 mutant, MDM2-amplified, ATM-null, NF-kB-hyperactivated) --- and does it correctly rank the radio-sensitivity of clinically-relevant cell lines (A549 wt-p53, H1299 p53-null, MCF-7 wt-p53, HCT116 p53-KO isogenic pair, U-87 wt-ATM vs U-87 ATM-KD)?
basis: The paper validates only on 'Ctr-RNAi vs Wip1-RNAi' in a single MCF-7-like background. It never tests whether the framework generalizes to the p53-mutant or ATM-null tumor backgrounds that dominate real oncology practice. This is arguably the single largest gap between the paper's mechanistic value and its clinical relevance. Our replication trivially inherits this untested boundary.
next_steps: For each of {TP53-null, MDM2-amp (5x k_mdm2), ATM-null (k_ATM_act -> 0), constitutive-NF-kB (5x baseline NFKBn)}, run the 6-dose sweep and predict clonogenic survival ranking. Compare against published radiosensitivity for the corresponding isogenic pairs: HCT116 p53+/+ vs p53-/- (Bunz et al. 1999), A549 vs H1299, MCF-7 vs T47D, U-87 wt vs U-87 ATM-KD. Score with Spearman rank correlation. If the model fails to rank correctly, the missing ingredients are almost certainly (i) DNA-repair-pathway choice (HR vs NHEJ) which is not modelled, and (ii) mitotic-catastrophe fate which is lumped into apoptosis here.
